entities.label: mp_Attribution
entities.description:
### Definition
`mp_Attribution` is the technical schema label used for an MP Attribution: a provenance/qualifier Representation that records who is responsible for, asserted, created, curated, or otherwise accounts for another Representation. The Attribution is not itself the responsible person or organization.

### Extract when
Create an Attribution only when the text explicitly identifies an accountable person, author group, institution, laboratory, project, or authority in relation to a Claim, Statement, DataSet, Method, or Reference.

### Do not extract when
Do not create an Attribution for vague agency such as “researchers believe” or “it is known” when no accountable source is identifiable. Do not infer authorship from document metadata unless the extraction passage explicitly supports that attribution.

### Relations
In this schema, an Attribution may `mp_supports` the Representation whose provenance/responsibility it qualifies, reflecting the Micropublication minimal-support interpretation of attribution.

### Example
“According to the NOM-Lab at Southwest University, DOM fluorescence was measured using EEM spectroscopy.” -> Attribution[NOM-Lab], supporting the relevant Method/DataSet/Statement representation.

entities.label: mp_References
entities.description:
### Definition
`mp_References` is the Neo4j-compatible technical label used in this schema for the canonical Micropublication class `mp:Reference`. A Reference represents an explicitly cited external bibliographic source, dataset citation, DOI, URL, or other identifiable source record.

### Extract when
Create one Reference per explicitly identifiable cited source, including author–year citations, numbered citations, DOI/URL references, or a bibliographic entry linked to the current passage.

### Do not extract when
Do not create a Reference for vague phrases such as “previous studies” unless an identifiable source is provided. Do not merge multiple cited works into one Reference node.

### Relations
Use `cito_isCitedBy` from the Reference to the Representation that cites it. Use `mp_supports` to a Claim or Statement only when the cited source is explicitly invoked as backing for that proposition; a neutral citation alone does not imply support.

### Example
“Biochar can reduce Hg bioavailability (Smith et al., 2020).” -> Reference[Smith et al., 2020]; Reference `cito_isCitedBy` Statement/Claim; add `mp_supports` only if the text uses the source as evidential backing.

entities.label: whu_Computational_Experiment
entities.description:
### Definition
A `whu_Computational_Experiment` is a mid-level planned analytical module for statistical, computational, modeling, or transformation procedures applied primarily to data. It is represented as a Plan/organized semantic unit, not as a single atomic step.

### Extract when
Create one when the passage describes a coherent computational analysis such as regression, PCA, ANOVA, machine learning, simulation, or statistical modeling that contains one or more `whu_ResearchStep` instances.

### Relations
ResearchStep instances belong to it via `p_plan_isStepOfPlan`, use Method/Software via `whu_declaredUsed`, and consume/produce DataSet entities via `whu_declaredInput`/`whu_declaredOutput`. `whu_fellow(X,Y)` means Y is the immediate upstream predecessor/provider of X.

### Example
“PCA and Kruskal–Wallis tests were conducted in R 4.2.2.” -> Computational_Experiment with Computational ResearchStep(s), declaredUsed Software[R 4.2.2].

entities.label: envo_EnvironmentMaterial
entities.description:
### Definition
`envo_EnvironmentMaterial` is the Neo4j schema label used here for an ENVO-aligned environmental material: a material matrix or medium such as soil, sediment, water, air, or particulate matter.

### Extract when
Create an EnvironmentMaterial when the text explicitly names the environmental substance or matrix from which specimens are collected or with which they interact.

### Distinguish from
Do not use this class for a bounded site or environmental setting; use `whu_EnvironmentFeature`. Do not use it for the collected sample itself; use `whu_Specimen`.

### Relations
`whu_EnvironmentFeature -> bfo_has_part -> envo_EnvironmentMaterial`; a Specimen may `prov_wasDerivedFrom` the material; the material may `bfo_has_part` a `whu_ChemicalEntity`.

### Example
“Surface soil was collected from the paddy field.” -> EnvironmentFeature[paddy field] has_part EnvironmentMaterial[surface soil].

### Definition
A `whu_Reagent` is a chemical or biological reagent, standard, solution, reference material, buffer, or other consumable explicitly used in a recorded research step.

### Extract when
Create a Reagent when the passage names the reagent or gives identifying details such as concentration, grade, supplier, or formulation.

### Relations

### Example
“Samples were digested with 65% suprapure HNO3.” -> Reagent[65% suprapure HNO3].

entities.label: iao_ScalarMeasurementDatum
entities.description:
### Definition
An `iao_ScalarMeasurementDatum` is a scalar measurement datum represented by a single numeric magnitude together with its measurement unit; it is treated as a subtype of `iao_DataItem`.

### Extract when
Use this class when the passage reports a specific scalar value such as “28.4 ng/g”, optionally with an explicit comparator. If the record is categorical, composite, or not reducible to one scalar value plus unit, use `iao_DataItem`.

### Relations
Link to the measured/analyzed `whu_TargetVariable` via `iao_is_about`. A DataSet contains DataItem-level records via `dcterms_hasPart`.

### Example
“Mean THg concentration was 28.4 ng/g.” -> ScalarMeasurementDatum[value=28.4, unit=ng/g] is_about TargetVariable[THg concentration].

properties.name: whu_hascomparator
properties.description: Extract only an explicit comparison operator or qualifier attached to the scalar value, e.g. '<', '<=', '>', '>=', '=', 'approximately'. Return null/omit when no comparator is stated.

properties.name: iao_hasMeasurementUnit
properties.description: Extract the measurement unit exactly as written in the source text (e.g. ng/g, mg/L, %, °C). Do not convert or normalize units during extraction.

properties.name: iao_hasMeasurementValue
properties.description: Extract only the numeric magnitude as a FLOAT, excluding the unit and comparator. Preserve the reported numerical value; do not perform unit conversion.

### Definition
A `whu_Software` entity represents named software, a software package, computational environment, or analysis application explicitly used in a computational research step.

### Extract when

### Example
“Statistical analyses were performed in R version 4.2.2.” -> Software[R], version=4.2.2.

properties.name: whu_brand

properties.name: schema_softwareVersion
properties.description: Extract the software version/release exactly as stated (e.g. 4.2.2, 26, R2021b). Omit when no version is provided.

entities.label: whu_TargetVariable
entities.description:
### Definition
A `whu_TargetVariable` is the specific measurable, analyzable, or predictable quantity toward which a research Goal is directed, such as Hg concentration, MeHg content, methylation rate, or a model response variable.

### Extract when
Create a TargetVariable when the passage names a quantity or variable being measured, analyzed, compared, or predicted. Keep it distinct from the underlying substance itself.

### Relations
`whu_Goal -> whu_hasTarget -> whu_TargetVariable`; `whu_TargetVariable -> iao_is_about -> whu_ChemicalEntity`; DataSet/DataItem/ScalarMeasurementDatum may `iao_is_about` the TargetVariable at the granularity supported by the text.

### Example
“Hg concentration in rice grain was quantified.” -> TargetVariable[Hg concentration] is_about ChemicalEntity[Hg].

entities.label: whu_SpecimenCollection
entities.description:
### Definition
A `whu_SpecimenCollection` is a mid-level sampling Plan composed of one or more collection-type `whu_ResearchStep` instances and representing acquisition of a physical specimen from an environmental or biological source.

### Extract when
Create one when the passage describes a coherent sampling/collection procedure, including site, depth, timing, design, or sampling method.

### Relations
Collection ResearchSteps belong via `p_plan_isStepOfPlan` and produce `whu_Specimen` via `whu_declaredOutput`. The collection Plan links to its environmental context via `whu_hasContext`. At the plan-level shortcut view, an extracted Specimen may link back to the collection Plan through `p_plan_isOutputVarOf`.

### Example
“Topsoil (0–20 cm) was collected from paddy fields using a stainless-steel auger.” -> SpecimenCollection; SpecimenCollection hasContext EnvironmentFeature[paddy field]; ResearchStep[collection] declaredOutput Specimen[topsoil].

entities.label: mp_Claim
entities.description:
### Definition
An `mp_Claim` is a principal scientific assertion that functions as a focal proposition in the argumentation structure. It is more central and argumentative than a general `mp_Statement`.

### Extract when
Create a Claim when the passage explicitly presents a principal conclusion, hypothesis, interpretation, or scientific assertion that is supported or challenged by evidence or other propositions.

### Do not extract when
Use `mp_Statement` for ordinary factual observations, contextual assertions, or propositions that are not functioning as a focal argumentative claim.

### Relations
Claims may receive `mp_supports`/`mp_challenges` from DataSet, Statement, Reference, ScienceEvidence, or other allowed Representations according to the potential schema.

### Example
“Modified biochar significantly reduced MeHg production in paddy soil.” -> Claim[modified biochar reduces MeHg production].

entities.label: whu_Goal
entities.description:
### Definition
A `whu_Goal` is an explicitly stated scientific objective of a BioChemical or Computational Experiment.

### Extract when
Create a Goal only when an objective is linguistically supported, e.g., “to quantify”, “to assess”, “to compare”, “to determine”, or “to predict”.

### Do not extract when
Do not convert broad background motivation or an inferred purpose into a Goal.

### Relations
Experiment -> `whu_hasGoal` -> Goal; Goal -> `whu_hasTarget` -> TargetVariable.

### Example
“To quantify Hg concentration in rice grain.” -> Goal[quantify Hg concentration in rice grain].

entities.label: mp_Statement
entities.description:
### Definition
An `mp_Statement` is a complete proposition with evaluable semantic content, such as an observation, factual assertion, interpretation, or intermediate conclusion. A Claim is a specialized focal Statement.

### Extract when
Create a Statement when the passage expresses a complete proposition that may participate in support/challenge relations but is not best treated as the central Claim.

### Do not extract when
Do not create a Statement for topic fragments, headings, isolated noun phrases, or vague mentions without propositional content.

### Example
“Cadmium concentrations were higher in roots than in grains.” -> Statement[cadmium concentrations were higher in roots than grains].

entities.label: whu_BioChemical_Experiment
entities.description:
### Definition
A `whu_BioChemical_Experiment` is a mid-level planned experimental module in which physical/biological specimens are measured, assayed, chemically treated, or otherwise analyzed to generate scientific data.

### Extract when
Create one for a coherent laboratory/biochemical/analytical experimental unit containing one or more `whu_ResearchStep` instances.

### Relations
ResearchSteps belong via `p_plan_isStepOfPlan`; the Experiment may have a `whu_Goal`; its steps use Method/Device/Reagent through `whu_declaredUsed`, consume Specimen/ProcessedSpecimen through `whu_declaredInput`, and generate DataSet/ProcessedSpecimen through `whu_declaredOutput`. `whu_fellow(X,Y)` means Y is the immediate upstream predecessor/provider of X.

### Example
“THg and MeHg were quantified by CVAFS after acid digestion.” -> BioChemical_Experiment containing digestion/measurement ResearchSteps.

entities.label: whu_EnvironmentFeature
entities.description:
### Definition
A `whu_EnvironmentFeature` is a bounded, locatable environmental setting or site described in the paper, such as a specific paddy field, wetland, river reach, sampling station, or experimental field. It is aligned conceptually with ENVO environmental feature and is distinct from the material present at the site.

### Extract when
Create one when the passage identifies a concrete environmental setting/site that frames sampling, organism location, or a recorded field ResearchStep. Coordinates may be captured as properties when explicit.

### Relations
EnvironmentFeature -> `bfo_has_part` -> EnvironmentMaterial; SpecimenCollection -> `whu_hasContext` -> EnvironmentFeature; organism/ResearchStep may -> `prov_atLocation` -> EnvironmentFeature. A Specimen may also `prov_wasDerivedFrom` an EnvironmentFeature when the passage identifies the site/environmental feature itself as the provenance source and does not support a more specific material or organism source.

### Example
“Topsoil was sampled from the SWU paddy field (29.8°N, 106.4°E).” -> EnvironmentFeature[SWU paddy field].

properties.name: gn_population
properties.description: Extract an explicitly stated population count associated with the named geographic/environmental feature. Do not infer or look up population externally.

properties.name: geo_alt
properties.description: Extract explicit altitude/elevation as a numeric value. Use the value as stated; do not infer from coordinates.

properties.name: geo_lat
properties.description: Extract explicit latitude as a decimal numeric value when present in the text.

properties.name: geo_long
properties.description: Extract explicit longitude as a decimal numeric value when present in the text.

entities.label: mp_Method
entities.description:
### Definition
An `mp_Method` is a named or describable scientific method, protocol, analytical technique, statistical procedure, or standard represented as information content rather than as a physical device.

### Extract when
Create a Method for methods such as ICP-MS analysis, EPA 3052 digestion protocol, PCA, regression, or a named standard/procedure.

### Distinguish from
Use `whu_Device` for the physical instrument and `whu_Software` for the software implementation.

### Relations
Link from the using ResearchStep via `whu_declaredUsed`. A Method may be aggregated with a DataSet in `whu_ScienceEvidence` via `prov_hadMember`.

### Example
“Digestion followed EPA 3052.” -> Method[EPA 3052].

entities.description:
### Definition
A `whu_SpecimenPreprocessing` is a mid-level preparation Plan composed of one or more preprocessing-type ResearchSteps that transform a raw `whu_Specimen` into a `whu_ProcessedSpecimen`.

### Extract when
Create one for coherent preparation procedures such as drying, grinding, sieving, filtration, preservation, digestion, or extraction before downstream analysis.

### Relations
ResearchSteps belong via `p_plan_isStepOfPlan`; they use `whu_declaredInput` for the raw Specimen and `whu_declaredOutput` for the ProcessedSpecimen. `whu_fellow(X,Y)` means the upstream SpecimenCollection is Y when preprocessing X follows collection.

### Example
“Soils were air-dried, ground, and passed through a 2-mm sieve.” -> SpecimenPreprocessing with corresponding ResearchStep(s).

A `whu_ProcessedSpecimen` is a physical specimen after preprocessing and before or during downstream experimental analysis.

### Extract when
Create one when the text explicitly identifies a materially transformed/prepared sample such as dried soil, sieved powder, digest, extract, filtrate, or homogenized tissue.

ProcessedSpecimen -> `prov_wasDerivedFrom` -> Specimen. It is linked to ResearchSteps through `whu_declaredOutput` (produced by preprocessing) and `whu_declaredInput` (consumed by downstream analysis). “Dried and sieved soil powder was used for Hg determination.” -> ProcessedSpecimen[dried and sieved soil powder].

entities.label: whu_DataSet
entities.description:
### Definition
A `whu_DataSet` is a scientific data collection generated by or used in one or more ResearchSteps. In BAE it carries both dataset semantics and an evidential/argumentative role.

### Extract when
Create a DataSet when the passage explicitly reports a coherent data artifact such as a table, figure, measurement set, spectrum set, modeled result set, or analysis output.

### Relations
ResearchStep -> `whu_declaredInput`/`whu_declaredOutput` -> DataSet. At the plan-level shortcut view, a DataSet may `p_plan_isOutputVarOf` a Computational_Experiment where the text directly presents the experiment-level output. DataSet -> `dcterms_hasPart` -> DataItem.

`iao_is_about` may be used at two complementary levels:
- DataSet -> Reagent / Specimen / ProcessedSpecimen, when the dataset concerns those research resources;
- DataSet -> TargetVariable, when the dataset concerns a measured/analyzed target variable.
DataItem/ScalarMeasurementDatum may also `iao_is_about` TargetVariable at finer granularity.

ScienceEvidence -> `prov_hadMember` -> DataSet. A DataSet may directly `mp_supports`/`mp_challenges` a Claim or Statement only when the text explicitly establishes that argumentative relation.

### Example
“Figure 4 reports MeHg concentrations in rice tissues after biochar treatment.” -> DataSet[Figure 4 MeHg concentrations], which may be about the relevant Specimen and TargetVariable when those links are textually supported.

entities.label: whu_Specimen
entities.description:
### Definition
A `whu_Specimen` is a physical biological or environmental sample that has been collected for research and may be passed to downstream preparation or experiments.

### Extract when
Create a Specimen for an actually collected sample such as rice grain, fish tissue, surface soil sample, or river-water sample.

### Provenance
A Specimen may `prov_wasDerivedFrom` the source most specifically supported by the passage:
- `whu_EnvironmentFeature` when the site/environmental feature itself is stated as the source;
- `envo_EnvironmentMaterial` when the source matrix/substance is explicit;
- `obi_organism` when a living biological source is explicit.
Do not invent a more specific source than the text supports.

### Relations
ResearchSteps connect through `whu_declaredOutput` (collection) and `whu_declaredInput` (preprocessing/analysis). At the plan-level shortcut view, Specimen may `p_plan_isOutputVarOf` SpecimenCollection and `p_plan_isInputVarOf` SpecimenPreprocessing. A Specimen may also `bfo_has_part` a ChemicalEntity when physical presence is explicit.

### Example
“Soil samples were collected from the paddy field.” -> Specimen[soil samples] wasDerivedFrom EnvironmentFeature[paddy field] when no more specific source matrix is stated.

properties.name: WHU_HASNAME
properties.description: Return a concise canonical name for this entity, grounded only in the source text. Prefer a short noun phrase (typically 2–12 words), preserve meaningful scientific abbreviations and identifiers, and do not add information that is not stated or unambiguously recoverable from the text. entities.label: whu_ScienceEvidence
entities.description:
### Definition
A `whu_ScienceEvidence` is a reusable composite evidence unit that binds at least one DataSet with the Method used to produce or analyze it in an explicit argumentative context. It bridges EEM experimental-process representation and MPU argumentation.

### Extract when
Create ScienceEvidence only when the passage contains (1) identifiable data/results, (2) the relevant method or analytical basis, and (3) an explicit or unambiguous argumentative role supporting or challenging a Claim/Statement. Raw data alone are a DataSet, not ScienceEvidence.

### Relations
ScienceEvidence -> `prov_hadMember` -> DataSet/Method. It may `mp_supports`/`mp_challenges` an explicit Claim or Statement. In this BAE schema it may also `mp_supports`/`mp_challenges` a SupportGraph to encode the evidence polarity within that graph; membership in the SupportGraph is separately represented by `prov_hadMember`.

### Extraction boundary
`WHU_HASORIGINALTEXT` should be the smallest contiguous span containing the evidential content and the argumentative connector. Do not infer ScienceEvidence solely from co-occurrence of a Method and DataSet.

### Example
“CVAFS measurements showed a 42% decrease in grain MeHg, supporting the biochar-remediation hypothesis.” -> ScienceEvidence[CVAFS evidence of reduced grain MeHg].

entities.label: whu_ResearchStep
entities.description:
### Definition
A `whu_ResearchStep` is the unified minimal semantic unit for an atomic research step recorded in the paper. It is modeled as both `p-plan:Step` and an information-content representation of the described step.

### Extract when
Create one for an explicit atomic operation belonging to one of four categories: SpecimenCollection, SpecimenProcessing, BioChemical, or Computational.

### Relations
ResearchStep -> `whu_declaredUsed` -> Method/Device/Reagent/Software; -> `whu_declaredInput`/`whu_declaredOutput` -> Specimen/ProcessedSpecimen/DataSet; -> `p_plan_isStepOfPlan` -> the corresponding mid-level Plan/Experiment; -> `p_plan_isPrecededBy` -> its immediate/explicit predecessor; and, when location is explicit, -> `prov_atLocation` -> EnvironmentFeature.

BAE reuses P-PLAN for Plan/Step organization and ordering. Domain-specific input/output links are represented directly by `whu_declaredInput` and `whu_declaredOutput`; P-PLAN `hasInputVar/hasOutputVar` are not used in this extraction schema.

`p_plan_correspondsToStep` is reserved for cases where an external provenance stage provides an explicit executed `prov:Activity`.

### Example
“After sieving, soil was digested with HNO3 and Hg was measured by CVAFS.” -> separate ResearchSteps for sieving, digestion, and measurement, linked by `p_plan_isPrecededBy`.

entities.label: obi_organism
entities.description:
### Definition
`obi_organism` is the current technical schema label for a living biological source explicitly mentioned in the paper, such as a plant, animal, or microorganism from which a specimen is obtained or whose environmental location is relevant.

### Extract when
Create an organism node when a living source is explicitly identified, rather than only a collected tissue/sample or an environmental material.

### Relations
Specimen -> `prov_wasDerivedFrom` -> organism; organism -> `prov_atLocation` -> EnvironmentFeature; organism -> `bfo_has_part` -> ChemicalEntity when the text explicitly describes a constituent present in the organism.

### Example
“Rice plants grown in the paddy field were sampled for grain and root tissue.” -> organism[rice plant]; Specimen[grain/root] wasDerivedFrom organism.

entities.label: whu_ChemicalEntity
entities.description:
### Definition
A `whu_ChemicalEntity` is a specific chemical element, compound, ion, or chemically identifiable substance explicitly named in the paper, with normalization to ChEBI where appropriate.

### Extract when
Create a ChemicalEntity when the text names the underlying substance itself (e.g., Hg, MeHg, Pb, Cd), not merely a measured variable such as “Hg concentration”.

### Relations
Specimen, organism, or EnvironmentMaterial may `bfo_has_part` a ChemicalEntity when the text supports physical presence. TargetVariable -> `iao_is_about` -> ChemicalEntity links a measured/analyzed quantity to its underlying substance.

### Example
“Total mercury and methylmercury concentrations were measured.” -> ChemicalEntity[Hg], ChemicalEntity[MeHg]; separate TargetVariables represent their concentrations.

entities.label: whu_SupportGraph
entities.description:
### Definition
A `whu_SupportGraph` is a mid-level argumentative aggregate organized around one focal `mp_Claim`. It is modeled as a Representation, information-content entity, and `prov:Collection`.

### Extract/construct when
Create one for a focal Claim that has explicit supporting or challenging argumentative material. The SupportGraph organizes the Claim together with relevant Statements, Attributions, References, and ScienceEvidence.

### Relations
SupportGraph -> `prov_hadMember` -> Claim/Statement/Attribution/Reference/ScienceEvidence. ScienceEvidence may `mp_supports`/`mp_challenges` the SupportGraph to encode its polarity with respect to the graph’s focal Claim. `prov_hadMember` records membership only; it does not itself encode argumentative polarity.

### Example
A Claim about biochar reducing MeHg may be represented by one SupportGraph containing the Claim, supporting ScienceEvidence, cited References, and explanatory Statements.

entities.label: iao_DataItem
entities.description:
### Definition
An `iao_DataItem` is an individually reportable information-content item contained within a DataSet, including categorical records, counts, concentrations, statistical summaries, or other data records. `iao_ScalarMeasurementDatum` is used for the more specific single-value-plus-unit case.

### Extract when
Create a DataItem when a distinct reportable record is present but cannot or should not be represented as a single scalar measurement datum.

### Relations
DataSet -> `dcterms_hasPart` -> DataItem; DataItem may -> `iao_is_about` -> TargetVariable.

### Example
“Soil pH was classified as acidic, neutral, or alkaline across sites.” -> DataItem[pH classification].
